title: Red Leicester Mac and Cheese
summary: A creamy, saucy hob-top mac and cheese, mostly Red Leicester with a little cheddar, Grana Padano, ricotta and feta. Never baked, so never stringy.

steps.text: Cook the macaroni in salted water until about 1 minute before al dente. Keep the pasta water before you drain it.
Meanwhile, melt the butter over a medium-low heat. Add the flour and stir constantly for {timer:1-2}, without letting it brown.
Add the milk slowly, whisking as you go. Cook it gently for {timer:3-5}, stirring, until it coats the back of a spoon. Do not make it very thick.
Add the Red Leicester in 3-4 batches, stirring gently between each, then the cheddar and the Grana Padano. Once smooth, stir in the ricotta, then crumble in the feta.
Season with black pepper and the nutmeg or cayenne, if using. Taste before adding any salt: the cheeses are salty.
Add the pasta and mix. It will look quite saucy at first, which is right: after a minute or two the pasta soaks some of it up. If it gets too thick, add pasta water a tablespoon at a time.
Serve it straight from the saucepan. Do not keep heating it once the cheese is in.

tips: Heat is what makes cheese stringy and tight. Taking the sauce off the heat before the cheese goes in, and never baking it, keeps it creamy and flowing with only a very slight pull.
For an even creamier sauce, use about 425 ml milk rather than more cheese. Keep 20-30 g extra Red Leicester to hand, and stir it in off the heat if the sauce needs more.
It makes 3 large or 4 normal portions.
